title: Follow the trace across hops, and keep the volume down
brief: A request crosses a gateway, an agent, an MCP server and a peer agent. Some hops split the trace, and the bill for traces keeps growing. Decide how context travels, where it breaks, and what you sample. The dials are not given.

blocks.title: One request, three kinds of hop
blocks.alt: A client calls an agent service over HTTP with a traceparent header. The agent calls an MCP server with traceparent inside params._meta. The agent calls a peer agent over HTTP with a traceparent header.
blocks.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant A as Agent service
  participant M as MCP server
  participant P as Peer agent
  C->>A: HTTP with traceparent header
  A->>M: tools/call with params._meta traceparent
  M-->>A: result
  A->>P: A2A over HTTP with traceparent header
  P-->>A: task result
blocks.caption: Every arrow is a place where the trace can split. Topic w15-t05.
How context crosses each hop
head: Hop
Carrier and rule
What to check
rows: Service to service over HTTP
W3C `traceparent` and `tracestate` headers. Trace Context Level 1 is a Recommendation (2021-11-23), Level 2 a Candidate Recommendation Draft (2024-03-28) [[r8]]
Gateways and proxies must forward the headers
Agent to MCP server

W3C `traceparent`, `tracestate` and `baggage` in `params._meta`, with unprefixed keys. MCP revision 2026-07-28 reserves them as an exception to the vendor-prefix rule [[r6]] [[r7]]. The MCP client span is the parent of the server span whatever the transport

Agent Framework Python injects them for sessions it opens (`MCPStreamableHTTPTool`, `MCPStdioTool`, `MCPWebsocketTool`) and not for hosted tools such as `get_mcp_tool(...)` or Foundry toolboxes. The docs describe this only for Python [[r10]]
Agent to A2A peer

HTTP headers. The A2A guidance says clients and servers should participate in distributed tracing with W3C Trace Context and should log task, session and correlation ids. The spec defines no tracing fields [[r9]]
Agent Framework's A2A client and server forwarding is not documented, so test it
Async hops (queue, background response, durable resume)
No source here. General OpenTelemetry practice is to carry `traceparent` in message properties and start a linked span
Verify with a test. Resumed work often starts a new trace

blocks.caption: Shape only. The identifier values are the W3C specification's example. Format: 00-<32 hex trace id>-<16 hex parent id>-<2 hex flags>.

blocks.text: Sampling: keep traces whole, keep the totals honest

blocks.caption: Sampling options (topic w15-t07)
head: Option
Decides
Wins when
Loses when
rows: Fixed-ratio head sampling, for example 0.05
At the root, from the trace id, so whole traces are kept [[r20]]. Python: `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG`, not the older `sampling_ratio` and `traces_per_second` [[r15]]
Traffic is high and uniform. If unsure, the vendor tip is to start at 5 percent
It cannot guarantee that every error or slow trace is kept
Rate-limited head sampling
The Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro default is five traces per second for Azure Monitor export [[r15]]
You want a hard cap on cost
Bursts above the rate are dropped, so load tests look incomplete
Tail sampling in a collector
After most or all spans of the trace have arrived [[r20]]
You must keep every error, every slow run or runs with a given attribute
Compute and engineering cost. The Agent Framework docs do not cover it
Metrics, which are not sampled
Every call is counted
Alerts, rates and cost totals
No per-run detail

blocks.title: Estimate totals from sampled spans
blocks.expr: estimated total = sum( value x itemCount ) over the retained spans

vars.v: how many original items one retained item stands for, about 1 / sampling ratio
the attribute you sum, for example gen_ai.usage.input_tokens

blocks.example: At a 10 percent ratio itemCount is about 10, so 300 retained spans of 1,000 input tokens each stand for 300 x 1,000 x 10 = 3,000,000 tokens. Application Insights stores `itemCount` on every retained item, and the Learn query `RetainedPercentage = 100/avg(itemCount)` shows how much is kept. Counters from metrics need no weighting.

blocks.title: Where traces break and numbers lie

items.symptom: A trace stops at the agent's `execute_tool` span and the MCP server's spans start separate traces.
items.cause: The tool is a hosted or provider-managed MCP tool, so the provider runtime makes the call and Agent Framework does not inject `params._meta`.
items.fix: Use a client-opened MCP transport where you need end-to-end traces, or join the two sides by `gen_ai.conversation.id` and accept the gap.

items.symptom: A load test shows far fewer traces than requests.
items.cause: The rate-limited default of five traces per second drops bursts.
items.fix: Use a fixed ratio, or raise the rate, for tests. Do not read the trace count as a request count.

items.symptom: The traces you wanted, the errors, are missing.
items.cause: Head sampling decided before the error happened.
items.fix: Add tail sampling in a collector for errors and slow runs, and alert from metrics, which are not sampled.

items.symptom: Token totals computed from spans are far too low.
items.cause: Retained spans were summed without weighting by `itemCount`.
items.fix: Weight by `itemCount`, or use the usage counters (level w15-l4).

items.symptom: The peer agent's work appears as a separate trace.
items.cause: Nothing forwarded `traceparent` over the A2A hop. The A2A spec has no tracing fields and the Agent Framework docs do not say whether its A2A client forwards the header.
items.fix: Test with a known `traceparent` and look for its trace id in the peer's spans. Log task and correlation ids as the A2A guidance advises [[r9]].

quiz.q: Put the steps of trace propagation across an MCP tool call in order.
items: The agent has an active span when it issues `tools/call`
The server extracts them and uses them as the remote parent
The server's span joins the same trace beneath the client span
quiz.explain: An active span must exist to have a context to inject. The client writes it into `params._meta`, the server reads it as the remote parent, and its own span then becomes part of the trace.

quiz.q: Traces are head-sampled at a fixed ratio of 5 percent, so `itemCount` is about 20. In one hour, 500 retained chat spans carry an average of 2,000 `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` each. Estimate the real input tokens for the hour.
quiz.hint: Weight each retained span by itemCount.
quiz.explain: Each retained span stands for about 20 original spans, so the estimate is 500 x 2,000 x 20 = 20,000,000 tokens. Summing the retained spans alone gives 1,000,000, which is 20 times too low. A usage counter would have given the exact figure without weighting.

quiz.q: An agent calls a Foundry-hosted MCP tool through `get_mcp_tool(...)`. Traces end at the agent's `execute_tool` span and the MCP server's spans start separate traces. Why?
options: Head sampling dropped the MCP server's spans, because each service applies its own sampling ratio and the server's ratio was lower
MCP forbids `traceparent` in `_meta` because of its vendor-prefix rule for unregistered keys
A hosted tool is called by the provider runtime, so no `params._meta` is injected. Use a client-opened MCP transport
`baggage` must be set first, because the server accepts `traceparent` only when baggage is present
quiz.explain: Agent Framework injects trace context only for MCP sessions the agent process opens. A hosted tool is invoked by the provider's runtime. MCP reserves `traceparent` in `_meta` as an exception to the vendor-prefix rule, baggage is optional, and head sampling would cut whole traces, not split them.

takeaways: A trace crosses a hop only if something carries the context: HTTP headers between services, `params._meta` for MCP, headers for A2A.
Hosted or provider-managed MCP tools are called by the provider, so the chain breaks there. Use a client-opened transport for end-to-end traces.
Head sampling is cheap and cannot keep every error. Tail sampling can, at a cost. Metrics are never sampled, so alert from them.
Weight sums over sampled spans by `itemCount`, or use counters, and treat the A2A forwarding as untested until you test it.
